source_title: Travis Perkins Annual Report and Accounts 2019 - Wickes segment
availability_evidence: Travis Perkins annual report pages 71 and 134 state that the parent strategic report and financial statements containing the Wickes segment disclosure were approved by the Board on 2 March 2020; issuer-hosted report bytes are hash-preserved locally.
observation: The Wickes segment delivered a strong recovery: revenue rose 7.4% to £1,342m, like-for-like sales increased 8.6%, adjusted operating profit grew 26% to £97m, adjusted margin expanded 100bps to 7.2% and return on capital employed improved to 7%. The parent Group also reported strong cash generation, while the planned Wickes demerger was already well progressed.
already_announced_exclusion: The announced Wickes demerger, prior overhead reductions, store-network actions and other self-help measures disclosed before cutoff are excluded from any future target event.
review_note: Strong segment revenue, profit, margin and return-on-capital growth provide exceptionally strong contrary evidence. The demerger is an already-announced corporate action rather than a future target.

source_title: Wickes Group Annual Report and Accounts 2021
availability_evidence: Annual report pages 68 and 113 state that the strategic report and financial statements were approved by the Board on 24 March 2022; issuer-hosted report bytes are hash-preserved locally.
observation: Revenue rose 14% to £1,534.9m, like-for-like sales increased 13%, adjusted operating profit grew to £116.3m from £81.6m, adjusted margin expanded to 7.6% and adjusted profit before tax increased 71.7% to £85.0m. Year-end net cash rose to £123.4m, IFRS net debt fell to £618.7m and leverage improved to 2.8x despite inventory investment and separation costs.
already_announced_exclusion: The completed demerger, IT separation programme, listing-related costs, store refits and other previously disclosed separation or investment actions are excluded from any future target event.
review_note: Exceptional revenue, profit and margin growth, strong net cash and falling IFRS debt provide exceptionally strong contrary evidence. Inventory investment and residual separation execution create only limited cash pressure.

source_title: Wickes Group Annual Report and Accounts 2023
availability_evidence: Annual report pages 85 and 143 state that the strategic report and financial statements were approved by the Board on 18 March 2024; issuer-hosted report bytes are hash-preserved locally.
observation: Revenue was broadly flat at £1,553.8m and like-for-like sales declined 0.3%. Adjusted operating profit fell 29% to £73.8m, adjusted margin contracted to 4.7% from 6.7% and adjusted profit before tax fell 31% to £52.0m amid wage, energy and demand pressure. Statutory profit before tax rose slightly to £41.1m, free cash flow increased to £46.1m and year-end net cash remained strong at £97.5m, although IFRS leverage increased to 3.3x.
already_announced_exclusion: The concluded Travis Perkins IT separation, £22m productivity programme, store closures, impairment actions and current business-change programme disclosed before cutoff are excluded from any future target event.
review_note: Sharp adjusted profit and margin deterioration and higher lease leverage create high operating pressure. Positive statutory profit, improved free cash flow and a substantial net cash balance provide meaningful contrary evidence.
